The checked-in source catalogue is the discoverable parser contract:

```{r}
catalogue <- readreq::req_source_catalog()
table(catalogue$source_dataset, catalogue$parser_family)
```

Forecast families are overview, quarterly and commodity. Historical families
are annual, quarterly, monthly, commodity detail and export markets. Commodity
profiles retain world/Australia sections, multiple products, geography, units
and nominal/real price rows.

`sheets` and `tables` accept stable `table_id` values or documented source
aliases:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
iron <- read_req_forecasts(
  "req-2026-06",
  sheets = c("forecast_iron_ore", "Quarterly prices")
)
monthly <- read_req_history(
  "req-2026-06",
  tables = "history_monthly_benchmark_prices"
)
```

The parser accounts for every non-empty value inside a recognized period grid.
Control markers are explicitly diagnosed; unexplained text in a numeric region
is an error.
